attempts.summary: Built redundant Layer-3 transit between node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense), which each front a private network hosting node3 and node4 respectively. Discovered the physical topology by ARP-probing unassigned interfaces (node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 = transit-A, node1 eth2<->node2 vtnet2 = transit-B, node1 eth3<->node3 = private net 1, node2 vtnet3<->node4 = private net 2). Assigned static addressing (10.10.11.0/30, 10.10.12.0/30 transits; 10.10.1.0/24, 10.10.2.0/24 private nets) and ran OSPF via VyOS's native protocol stack and OPNsense's os-frr plugin so both routers form dual Full adjacencies and install ECMP routes to each other's private subnet. Demonstrated the failover requirement live: started a continuous ping from node3 to node4, administratively shut down transit-A on node1, confirmed OSPF withdrew that path within seconds with zero packet loss in the ping stream (43 sequential replies, no gaps), then restored transit-A and confirmed both OSPF adjacencies and ECMP paths came back. Finally ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (node1 VyOS reboot, node2 OPNsense shutdown -r, node3/node4 systemctl reboot), verifying each node's boot identity changed (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD) and that its configuration, OSPF adjacencies, and end-to-end reachability recovered after each restart before proceeding to the next node. One self-inflicted issue was caught and fixed mid-task: a cleanup `ip addr flush` on node1 briefly wiped its real transit/private addresses (not just leftover discovery IPs); this was corrected by deleting and re-setting the VyOS interface addresses and re-committing, after which connectivity and OSPF fully recovered before the restart protocol began.
